criteria.text: The participant is 12 years of age or older

The participant has a histologically-proven locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor, multiple myeloma or B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma and is no longer benefiting from standard anti-cancer treatment or for whom, in the opinion of the treating physician, no such treatment is available or indicated
The participant has a Performance status of 0-2 (Per Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) criteria)
The participant has acceptable organ function as defined below
The participant has an Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 1500 µl
The participant has a Hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dl
The participant has Platelets ≥ 75,000/µl
The participant has a Total bilirubin < 2.0 mg/ dl, except in patients with Gilbert's Syndrome

The participant has Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (SGPT) < 2.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN) (or < 5 x ULN in patients with known hepatic metastases)
The participant has Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5 × ULN or calculated or measured creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min/1.73 m2

The participant has disease that can be objectively measured by physical, laboratory or radiographic exam (per RECIST v1.1 for solid tumor, Lugano criteria for non-Hodgkin lymphoma or International Myeloma Working Group criteria for multiple myeloma)

Results must be available from a genomic test or immunohistochemistry (IHC) test for protein expression performed in a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-certified and College of American Pathologists (CAP)-accredited or New York State accredited (for labs offering services to residents of NY) laboratory
The participant has the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent/assent document

The participant has a tumor genomic profile for which single agent treatment with one of the FDA approved targeted anti-cancer drugs included in this study has potential clinical benefit based on the criteria described in protocol
The patient must be able to swallow and tolerate oral medication and must have no known malabsorption syndrome

Women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) for the duration of study participation, and for four months following completion of study therapy
The participant's disease is not measurable or cannot be assessed by radiographic imaging or physical examination (e.g., elevated serum tumor marker only)
The participant has primary brain tumors or new, untreated or progressive leptomeningeal metastases

The participant has previously treated brain metastases or previously treated leptomeningeal disease and has not experienced a seizure or had a clinically significant change in neurological status within the 1 months prior to registration, and is clinically stable for at least 1 month after completion of treatment and off steroid treatment for one month prior to study enrollment
The participant has known progressive brain metastases

P1.text: 12 years of age or older (\*Restrictions apply. Not all therapies are available for patients \<18)

P2.text: Histologically-proven locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor, multiple myeloma or B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma who is no longer benefiting from standard anti-cancer treatment or for whom, in the opinion of the treating physician, no such treatment is available or indicated (except under the circumstance in which the TAPUR arm is designed to provide additional evidence to support an existing FDA indication).

P3.text: Performance status 0-2 (Per Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) criteria)

P4.text: Patients must have acceptable organ function as defined below. However, as noted above, drug-specific inclusion/exclusion criteria specified in the protocol appendix for each agent will take precedence for this and all inclusion criteria:

P8.text: 4. Total bilirubin \< 2.0 mg/ dl, except in patients with Gilbert's Syndrome

P9.text: 5. Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (SGPT) \< 2.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN) (or \< 5 x ULN in patients with known hepatic metastases)

P10.text: 6. Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5 × ULN or calculated or measured creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min/1.73 m2

P11.text: Patients must have disease that can be objectively measured by physical, laboratory or radiographic exam (per RECIST v1.1 for solid tumor, Lugano criteria for non-Hodgkin lymphoma or International Myeloma Working Group criteria for multiple myeloma).

P12.text: Results must be available from a genomic test or immunohistochemistry (IHC) test for protein expression performed in a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-certified and College of American Pathologists (CAP)-accredited or New York State accredited (for labs offering services to residents of NY) laboratory. Labs that have registered the test with the NIH Genetic Testing Registry or that provide a report that has been designated as optimized for TAPUR participation are preferred, but not required. The genomic or IHC test used to qualify a patient for participation in TAPUR may have been performed on any specimen of the patient's tumor obtained at any point during the patient's care at the discretion of the patient's treating physician. Genomic assays performed on cell-free DNA in plasma ("liquid biopsies") will also be acceptable if the genomic analysis is performed in a laboratory that meets the criteria described above.

P13.text: Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent/assent document.

P14.text: Have a tumor genomic profile for which single agent treatment with one of the FDA approved targeted anti-cancer drugs included in this study has potential clinical benefit based on the criteria described in protocol.

P15.text: For orally administered drugs, the patient must be able to swallow and tolerate oral medication and must have no known malabsorption syndrome.

P16.text: Because of the risks of drug treatment to the developing fetus, women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) for the duration of study participation, and for four months following completion of study therapy. Should a woman become pregnant or suspect she is pregnant while participating in this study or if she is the partner of a male participant in this study and becomes pregnant while he is participating in this study, she should inform her or her partner's treating physician immediately as well as her obstetrician. Female study patients who become pregnant must immediately discontinue treatment with any study therapy. Male patients should avoid impregnating a female partner. Male study patients, even if surgically sterilized, (i.e. post-vasectomy) must agree to one of the following: practice effective barrier contraception during the entire study treatment period and for a specified amount of time the last dose of study treatment, or completely abstain from sexual intercourse.

P17.text: Patients whose disease is not measurable or cannot be assessed by radiographic imaging or physical examination (e.g., elevated serum tumor marker only) are not eligible

P18.text: Patients with primary brain tumors or new, untreated or progressive leptomeningeal metastases are excluded

P19.text: Patients with previously treated brain metastases or previously treated leptomeningeal disease are eligible, provided that the patient has not experienced a seizure or had a clinically significant change in neurological status within the 1 months prior to registration. All patients with previously treated brain metastases must be clinically stable for at least 1 month after completion of treatment and off steroid treatment for one month prior to study enrollment.

P20.text: Patients with known progressive brain metastases are eligible but additional eligibility criteria apply.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "TAPUR: Testing the Use of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Approved Drugs That Target a Specific Abnormality in a Tumor Gene in People With Advanced Stage Cancer". Your earlier answers already covered 4 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you 12 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 82 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your recent blood tests showed that your liver, kidneys, and bone marrow are working well enough for this study? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the liver, kidneys, and bone marrow results. I know his cancer has spread to his liver, but I don't know if his blood tests are okay.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have results from a genomic or IHC test for your tumor that were done at a CLIA-certified lab?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I'd have to ask his doctor about the specific lab certifications for those tests.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document for this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can understand and I'm willing to sign the consent form.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Has your doctor ever mentioned that your tumor has a specific genetic abnormality that might respond to one of the targeted drugs in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. We don't know if his tumor has a specific genetic abnormality that would respond to those drugs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you able to swallow pills and take oral medication without issues?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, he can swallow pills fine. He's been taking them for his other conditions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a malabsorption syndrome, or do you have trouble tolerating oral medications (e.g., frequent nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea after taking them)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: He had bad diarrhea from the Keytruda, but that was colitis, not a stomach absorption problem. I don't know if he has any trouble tolerating pills now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. For this study, men and women of child-bearing potential must agree to use effective birth control (like condoms or hormonal methods) during the study and for 4 months after the last dose. Is he willing to do this?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, he is willing to use birth control. He's a man, so that's not an issue for him.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has your doctor confirmed that your cancer can be measured and tracked using scans (like CT or MRI) or physical exams, rather than just blood tests?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Neither of us knows, sorry. I'm not sure if the scans can measure it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any seizures or noticed any significant changes in your neurological status (like balance, vision, or strength) in the last month?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he hasn't had any seizures. I know his cancer hasn't spread to his brain, so I don't think he has those issues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has he ever been treated for cancer that spread to his brain or the fluid around it? Also, has he been stable for at least a month after that treatment and off steroid medications for one month before joining?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he has never been treated for cancer in the brain. We don't know about the lining of the brain or spinal cord, but I don't think he had treatment there.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has he been diagnosed with cancer that has spread to his brain (brain metastases)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, not in the brain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.

flags.reason: The message asserts that the patient can swallow pills and has been taking them for other conditions, but the facts do not contain this information and the persona is instructed to state uncertainty regarding his medications.
The message asserts that the person is willing to use birth control, which is a specific claim about his willingness and circumstances not stated in the facts.

The message claims the patient 'never been treated for cancer in the brain,' whereas the facts only state that the cancer has not spread to the brain (brain_mets), which is a different medical assertion than treatment history.
